harnessRecipes.title: Clipboard → Grok Expert
harnessRecipes.blurb: Whatever is on the macOS pasteboard becomes the auto-submitted prompt in Expert mode. Perfect after copying an error, email, or PR comment.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, urllib.parse
text = subprocess.check_output(["pbpaste"], text=True).strip()
assert text, "clipboard empty"
url = "https://grok.com/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(text) + "&mode=expert"
subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Safari", url], check=True)
print(url)
PY
harnessRecipes.notes: Uses the user's logged-in Safari profile — not an embedded bot browser.

harnessRecipes.title: Local file → Private Grok
harnessRecipes.blurb: Ship a log, dump, or notes file into a private auto-run so it does not stick in History the way normal ?q= chats do.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
FILE="/path/to/notes.md"
python3 - <<PY
import pathlib, urllib.parse, subprocess
p = pathlib.Path("$FILE")
body = p.read_text()[:12000]  # keep URL sane
prompt = f"Analyze this file ({p.name}):\n\n{body}"
url = "https://grok.com/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(prompt) + "&mode=expert#private"
subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Safari", url], check=True)
print("opened", len(prompt), "chars")
PY
harnessRecipes.notes: URL length limits still apply — truncate or summarize huge files first in Hermes, then open Grok for a second pass.

harnessRecipes.title: git diff → Expert review
harnessRecipes.blurb: From any repo working tree, open Grok on the unstaged (or staged) diff for a fast second-opinion review.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
cd /path/to/repo
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, urllib.parse
diff = subprocess.check_output(
    ["bash", "-lc", "git --no-pager diff | head -c 14000"], text=True
)
prompt = "Review this git diff. List bugs, risks, missing tests.\n\n" + diff
url = "https://grok.com/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(prompt) + "&mode=expert"
subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Safari", url], check=True)
print(url[:160], "…")
PY
harnessRecipes.notes: Hermes can run this in the project cwd. Prefer private hash if the diff is sensitive.

harnessRecipes.title: Open in already-authenticated Safari
harnessRecipes.blurb: Force the front Safari document (same cookies/session the human uses) instead of a cold browser profile.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
PROMPT='Summarize the last commit message style in this repo'
ENC=$(python3 -c "import urllib.parse,sys; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1]))" "$PROMPT")
URL="https://grok.com/?q=${ENC}&mode=fast"
osascript -e "tell application \"Safari\" to set URL of front document to \"$URL\""
harnessRecipes.notes: This is what the original experiment used. Embedded Browserbase sessions are often signed out.

harnessRecipes.title: computer_use: open + harvest reply
harnessRecipes.blurb: Hermes navigates grok.com in the desktop Safari window, waits for generation, then reads the AX tree / JS DOM for the reply text to paste into a report.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
# 1) Navigate (AppleScript or computer_use)
osascript -e 'tell application "Safari" to set URL of front document to "https://grok.com/?q=Say%20only%20READY&mode=fast"'
# 2) Wait for settle
sleep 8
# 3) Read back via JS in the authenticated page
osascript -e 'tell application "Safari" to do JavaScript "document.body.innerText.slice(0,2000)" in front document'
harnessRecipes.notes: Pair with a small observe.js helper (as in the param experiment) for structured JSON: url, modelLabel, privateState, reply snippet.

harnessRecipes.title: Re-run the param matrix under Hermes
harnessRecipes.blurb: Automated clean→one-param→observe→reset loop that writes fresh rows into data/findings.json when grok.com drifts.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
# Pseudocode Hermes loop (see methodology page)
for param in q mode m '#private' prompt model; do
  osascript -e "tell application \"Safari\" to set URL of front document to \"https://grok.com/\""
  sleep 2
  # load test URL for $param …
  # dump observe.js JSON → /tmp/obs_$param.json
  # merge into data/findings.json
done
harnessRecipes.notes: Keep tests on #private or disposable prompts so History is not flooded.

harnessRecipes.title: Cron: open a standing Grok brief
harnessRecipes.blurb: Hermes cron cannot “chat” as you inside Safari, but it can open a prepared deep link on a schedule (local-only deliver) so the tab is waiting when you sit down.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
# Hermes cron idea (local deliver):
# schedule: 0 9 * * 1-5
# script opens:
open -a Safari 'https://grok.com/?q=Morning%20brief%3A%20what%20should%20I%20prioritize%20today%20given%20my%20active%20projects&mode=expert'
harnessRecipes.notes: CLI cron deliver='local' saves output only — use open in a no_agent script for a pure URL launch with zero tokens.

harnessRecipes.title: Hermes draft → Grok second opinion
harnessRecipes.blurb: Hermes writes analysis locally (files, tests, math), then opens Grok with a compressed brief asking for contradictions and missing risks — dual-harness review.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
BRIEF=$(cat /tmp/hermes-brief.md | head -c 10000)
python3 -c '
import pathlib, urllib.parse, subprocess
brief = pathlib.Path("/tmp/hermes-brief.md").read_text()[:10000]
prompt = "Second opinion. List contradictions, missing risks, sharper claims.\n\n" + brief
url = "https://grok.com/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(prompt) + "&mode=expert"
subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Safari", url], check=True)
'
harnessRecipes.notes: Keep Hermes as lead; Grok is the adversarial reviewer. Use #private for unpublished research.

harnessRecipes.title: IDE / Terminal selection via pbcopy bridge
harnessRecipes.blurb: Select code in IntelliJ or Terminal, copy, then one Hermes command (or Finder-adjacent shell alias) fires Expert mode on that selection.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
# ~/.zshrc
grokq() {
  local mode="${1:-expert}"; shift || true
  local text
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then text="$*"; else text=$(pbpaste); fi
  local url="https://grok.com/?q=$(python3 -c 'import urllib.parse,sys; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.stdin.read()))' <<<"$text")&mode=${mode}"
  open -a Safari "$url"
}
# usage: copy code, then:  grokq expert
# or:  git diff | grokq   (if you adapt to read stdin)
harnessRecipes.notes: Tiny local affordance; Hermes can install the alias and verify with a dry-run echo of the URL.

harnessRecipes.title: Build-mode spike from a local spec
harnessRecipes.blurb: Open Grok in Build mode with a short product spec from a local markdown file — useful for UI/app spikes while Hermes keeps owning the repo.
harnessRecipes.snippet:
SPEC=./specs/spike.md
python3 -c '
import pathlib, urllib.parse, subprocess, sys
spec = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()[:8000]
prompt = "Build a minimal interactive prototype from this spec:\n\n" + spec
url = "https://grok.com/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(prompt) + "&mode=build"
subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Safari", url], check=True)
' "$SPEC"
harnessRecipes.notes: mode=build showed Build Beta UI in the live test; treat as observed, re-check if storage stickiness matters for your flow.

methodology.title: Clean state
methodology.detail: Navigate to https://grok.com/. Confirm authenticated session, empty composer, default model, Private control.

methodology.title: Discover candidates
methodology.detail: Inspect client bundles for URLSearchParams / routing (q, mode, m, fileid, #private, #planemodel). Add common guesses: prompt, model, temporary, private, side, voice, chat, rid.

methodology.title: One parameter at a time
methodology.detail: Load https://grok.com/?PARAM=VALUE (or hash/path). Record URL after settle, model label, private toggle, composer contents, auto-submit, History changes, localStorage modes-selected-id.

methodology.title: Reset
methodology.detail: Return to clean https://grok.com/ before the next candidate to avoid sticky mode/privacy bleed.

methodology.title: Combos & edges
methodology.detail: Test q+mode, q+#private, multiline %0A, long prompts, + vs %2B, empty/malformed q, mode refresh survival.

methodology.title: Cross-check modes
methodology.detail: POST /rest/modes in-page to list available mode ids and upgrade gates (Heavy).

methodology.title: Report only observations
methodology.detail: No speculation about server internals. Mark no-ops and unresolved cases explicitly.

discoveryNotes: Main prompt mount reads location.search q and optional fileid; non-empty q triggers handleSend with linkQuery, disableMemory, disablePersonalization.
Mode URL params tried in order: mode, then m — value must match an available mode id.
Hash #planemodel=(plane:…) calls setSelectedModeId without the availability gate.
Routing treats /chat and /c without id as temporary chat routes; after q submit, normal chats become /c/<uuid>?rid=….
